name: 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

profile.description: 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals develops and commercializes medicines to treat and prevent infectious diseases, with a focus on vector-borne illnesses. Its flagship product is ARAKODA (tafenoquine), the only FDA-approved once-weekly malaria prevention drug on the U.S. market. The company also has pipeline programs exploring tafenoquine for COVID-19, babesiosis, fungal pneumonias, and candidiasis.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The company's only commercial product, ARAKODA (tafenoquine), was FDA-approved for malaria prevention in 2018; the last five years have been about extending tafenoquine into babesiosis, an incremental extension rather than a new revenue stream [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI strategy or AI-enabled products identified [2]. Market Share (0/2): ARAKODA is the only once-weekly malaria prophylactic on the US market, but net product revenue of ~$208K in Q2 2026 shows negligible share of the travel-medicine category [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Three babesiosis trials are active with orphan drug status, and an interim hospital-study readout was guided for as early as late September 2026, but revenue visibility is absent [1][2]. R&D (0/1): R&D of $2.1M in FY2025 is tiny in absolute terms versus clinical-stage peers [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): The focus on medicines for vector-borne and infectious diseases, rooted in CEO Geoffrey Dow's 13 years in the Walter Reed/US Army antimalarial program, is clear but not yet validated by commercial impact [2]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable programs found. Employee Retention (0/2): ~25 employees and Dow serves as CEO, President and sole director — no retention data and concentrated governance [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider buying; instead shareholders approved success fees awarding management 5-6% of proceeds on a sale of ARAKODA or the company [3].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: ~379K average shares x $0.74 = ~$280K average daily dollar volume, below the $1M minimum, so Infrastructure = 0 regardless of other metrics. For reference, the mechanical score before the floor would have been ~3 (2.0/7): D/E of 5.8% scores 1.0 and TTM revenue growth of ~68% ($1.11M vs $0.66M) scores 1.0, while ROE of -212%, net margin of -730% and a 5-year revenue CAGR of -14.3% ($2.18M in 2020 to $1.01M in 2025) all score 0 [4]. Forward P/E and PEG are unavailable given continuing losses (~$2.4M net loss in Q2 2026) [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): An FDA-approved, patent-protected drug (malaria-indication exclusivity through 2035) with orphan drug status in babesiosis cannot be substituted by AI; the business is regulated, physical and clinical [2]. AI-accelerated drug discovery could speed competing antiparasitic programs over time, but that is a long-dated, indirect risk. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue [2].

infinite_game.summary: The founder's two-decade commitment to tafenoquine and the babesiosis push show some long-term intent, but the company now operates in survival mode — three reverse splits in about 18 months, a sole-director board and management success fees tied to selling ARAKODA [2][3]. Sinek would see a company playing not to run out of time rather than to advance a cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Bringing new treatments to underserved vector-borne diseases like babesiosis is a worthy aim tied to Dow's Army antimalarial background, but it reads as a product strategy and is now subordinate to asset monetization [2][3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A ~25-person team with the CEO as sole director, plus a shareholder vote with only 41.6% of shares represented approving management success fees and an 800K-share incentive-plan expansion, points to concentrated control rather than empowered teams [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of competitive self-reflection in company communications.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Repurposing tafenoquine from malaria prophylaxis into babesiosis, Lyme and fungal indications is genuine adaptation of the company's core asset [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management has kept funding three babesiosis trials and a Tulane research collaboration on Lyme and Bartonella despite a ~$2.6M market cap and repeated dilution [1][2].

investment_thesis: The bull case is binary: ARAKODA is an FDA-approved, once-weekly antimalarial with patent protection to 2035 and orphan designation in babesiosis, a growing tick-borne disease with no approved therapy, and net product revenue doubled (+106%) to ~$208K in Q2 2026 [1][2]. Positive interim data from the randomized hospital study or a sale of ARAKODA could be worth multiples of the ~$2.6M market cap.
thesis_continued: The bear case is severe: the company burns ~$2M+ per quarter against ~$1M of annual revenue, has done 1-for-12, 1-for-5 and 1-for-4 reverse splits since August 2024 to keep its Nasdaq listing, and the stock traded between $0.34 and $6 over the past year [1][3]. Average dollar volume of ~$280K fails IOWN's liquidity floor, governance is concentrated in a sole director, and management success fees on a sale create misaligned incentives [3].
key_catalysts: Interim analysis of the randomized babesiosis hospital study (guided for as early as late September 2026) [1]
Strategic sale or partnership for ARAKODA under the shareholder-approved monetization framework [3]
Continued triple-digit percentage growth in ARAKODA net product revenue [1]
key_risks: Going-concern and dilution risk from ~$2.3M quarterly operating expenses on ~$0.2M quarterly revenue [1]
Further reverse splits or Nasdaq delisting after three reverse splits since August 2024 [3]
Negative or delayed babesiosis trial results eliminating the main value driver [1][2]
